text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Thirty-five foreign-invested projects, with a capital of $918.14 million, were licensed to operate in Vietnam last month.
-- Tropical Storm Ernie, with winds of up to 74 km (46 miles) per hour, was expected to hit four central coast provinces at around midday on Friday.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam will leave on Saturday for a four-day visit to Australia.
-- A delegation from the National People's Congress of China, led by Chairman and member of the Politburo Standing Committee Qiao Shi, is expected to visit Vietnam soon.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong told the United Nations Food Summit in Rome that Vietnam will eliminate poverty and hunger by the year 2005.
-- The Swedish government pledged to lend Vietnam $54.9 million to finance the construction of the Song Hinh hydropower plan.
-- American Senator John McCain told reporters that Most-Favoured-Nation status was the next appropriate step in U.S-Vietnam relations and was among the top priorities of Washington's Vietnam policy.
